Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of present revision petition filed U/s 397 Cr.P.C. against the order dated 07.07.2022 passed by Ld. MM-04, South in Ct. Case No.31160/2019 titled as Ratan Lal Gupta Vs. Harish Sharma And Ors. whereby respondents were not summoned as accused for the alleged offences.

2. Briefly stated the facts as per record are as under:-
An application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. alongwith complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C. was filed by the revisionists against Mr. Harish Sharma, Mr. Dinesh Sharma (respondent no.1 herein) and Mr. Digvijay Pandey (respondent no.2 herein).
It was alleged that in the year 2014, revisionists were searching for shops for business purpose.
During that period, revisionist no.1 met respondent no.2 Mr. Digvijay Pandey who was working as a broker in real estate business.
It was further alleged that respondent no.2 introduced Mr. Harish Sharma and Mr. Dinesh Sharma to revisionist no.1 SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA

Date:
2024.01.16 17:26:51 +0530 who were builders by profession and they were developing and constructing the project of IT/ITES Office Space/ other facilities on a piece of land situated at Knowledge Park-5, Greater Noida, GB Nagar, U.P. Thereafter on 15.12.2014, revisionist no.1 alongwith respondent no.2 had gone to the registered office of company namely Aadhar Infra Holding Ltd. at 113, Vishal Tower, Janakpuri,
New Delhi-110058 where respondent no.2 introduced Mr. Harish Sharma as Director of Aadhar Infra Holding Ltd.
Respondent Mr. Dinesh Sharma was introduced as its Manager.

They both had shown a broucher of their project at Greater NOIDA and asked him to come alongwith his family members i.e., revisionist no.2 to 4 the next day so that they can show the site which they were going to sell to him.

On the next day, all the revisionists alongwith both the respondents went to Knowledge Park-5,
Greater NOIDA, U.P. to see the site of property.

On 26.12.2014, the revisionists went to the office of company where Mr. Harish Sharma and Mr. Dinesh Sharma told them that they were selling one retail shop measuring 200 sq.feet against which they were to pay total amount of Rs.6 lacs.
For booking of said shop, they were to pay about 50% of the total amount plus service tax and remaining 50% plus service tax was to be paid at the time of possession.
On 27.12.2014, respondent no.2 came to the house of revisionists at Chhatarpur Enclave to take the booking amount whereupon revisionist no.1 issued four cheques amounting to Rs.1 lac each.
On 06.01.2015, four separate demand letters were issued by the company to revisionists for paying balance of 50% of total amount i.e., Rs.2,11,124/- and same was paid on 18.01.2015

It was further alleged that thereafter, all the revisionists SUNIL by SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2024.01.16 17:26:59 +0530 entered into MoU for purchase of four separate properties with the said company through its Director/authorized signatory Mr.
Harish Sharma whereby it was assured that possession of the shop shall be handed over within 48 months from the date of booking.

Thereafter, four separate letters dated 01.01.2016 were sent by the company to the revisionists giving them an option sell their units/shops to the developer after a period of 48 months whereupon it was assured that the amount already paid alongwith an appreciation of Rs.2,70,000/- less TDS as applicable shall be returned.

Four post dated cheques (dated 18.02.2019)
amounting to Rs.5,43,000/- each were enclosed alongwith aforementioned letter.
After completion of 48 months, when the revisionists approached the accused persons for possession of their shops same was denied and they were allegedly threatened to kill.
For separate complaints dated 16.04.2019 were sent to concerned ACP as well as DCP in this regard, however no action was taken.
3. The matter came up for hearing on 30.09.2019.
After considering the ATR and material on record, Ld. MM dismissed the application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C vide order dated 21.08.2020.
Cognizance was taken on the complaint u/s 200 Cr.P.C. and matter was fixed for PSE for 14.10.2020.

Revisionist no.1 examined himself as CW-1 in pre-summoning evidence and thereafter,
PSE was closed vide his separate statement.

After considering the arguments and record, Ld.
Magistrate summoned Mr. Harish Sharma as an accused for the offence U/s 420 IPC and Section 506- II IPC.
Summoning of both the respondents herein was declined.

That order SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2024.01.16 17:27:08 +0530 is being challenged in these proceedings as far as same pertains to non- summoning of respondents.

4. Arguments heard from both the sides.
5.
It has been argued by Ld. Counsel for revisionists that Ld. Magistrate has committed an error in passing the impugned order as material on record was not properly appreciated.
It has been submitted that both the respondents had played an active role alongwith accused Harish Sharma in commission of alleged offences.
It has been submitted that revisionist no.1 had handed over all the cheques for making payment qua the shops to the respondents.
It has been further submitted that both the respondents had accompanied the revisionists to inspect the site.
It has been submitted that respondent no.2 has even witnessed the execution of MoUs between the parties.
Prayer has been made to set aside the impugned order to this limited extent and to summon the respondents as accused.
6. Per contra, it has been submitted by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 that present revision petition was not maintainable.

It has been submitted that the revisionist has put on record different Ratan Lal Gupta And Ors vs Harish Sharma And Ors on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64738874/
3 versions of sequence of events pertaining to commission of alleged offences.

sentences.text: 7. Similar submissions have been made by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2.
It has been submitted that he was merely a broker and he was not having any role in commission of alleged offences.
8. I have considered the submissions from both the sides alongwith record.
9. At first, this Court shall decide maintainability of present revision petition.

As per section 397(2)
Cr.P.C., the power of revision shall not be exercised in relation to any interlocutory order.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Amar Nath vs. State of Haryana, AIR 1977 SC 2185 has observed that the interlocutory order means orders of purely interim or temporary nature which do not decide or touch the important right or the liabilities of the parties and any order which substantially affects the right of the accused, or decides certain rights of the parties cannot be said to be an interlocutory order.

entities.text: Amar Nath vs. State of Haryana, AIR 1977 SC 2185
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was further observed that orders summoning SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2024.01.16 17:27:29 +0530 witnesses, adjourning cases, passing orders for bail,
calling for a report and such other steps in aid of pending proceedings, may no doubt,
amount to interlocutory orders, against which no revision would lie but orders which affect or adjudicate the rights of the accused or a particular aspect of the trial, cannot said to be interlocutory order.

By applying the said yardstick, it is clear that this revision petition was maintainable as impugned order whereby both the respondents were not summoned as accused was certainly final in nature qua them.
Judgments being relied upon by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 are distinguishable on facts.

10. On merits, Ld. Magistrate dealt with the aspect of summoning of respondents in the impugned order in following manner:-
"Accordingly, I come to conclusion that there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the respondent no.1, namely, Harish Sharma for the offence of cheating Ratan Lal Gupta And Ors vs Harish Sharma And Ors on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64738874/
4 punishable under Section 420 IPC and for offence of criminal intimidation.

entities.text: Ratan Lal Gupta And Ors vs Harish Sharma And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
there are no grounds to proceed against respondent no.2 and 3."
11.

As mentioned earlier, Ld. Counsel for revisionists has submitted that material on record was sufficient to show a prima facie case against the respondents so they should have been summoned as accused whereas Ld. Defence Counsels have submitted that there was no illegality in the impugned order as there was nothing on record against them.
Ld. Magistrate has simply observed in the impugned order that there were no grounds to proceed against the respondents.
It is not clear as to on what basis Ld. Magistrate arrived at such a conclusion.

Before giving such a finding, Ld.
Magistrate should have discussed the material on record SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2024.01.16 17:27:42 +0530 against them.
He could have declined their summoning as accused after that.
Such a course of action would have make it possible for the Courts exercising revisional jurisdiction to examine the reasoning given thereof which is not possible in the present case.
It is settled legal proposition that reasons are the heart and soul of any order.

12. Considering the above discussion, this Court is of the view that impugned order is liable to be set aside as far as same pertains to non- summoning of respondents Mr. Dinesh Sharma and Mr.
Digvijay Pandey.
Matter be put up before Ld. Magistrate on 23.01.2024 at 02:00 pm.
Ld. Magistrate is requested to pass a reasoned order on the aspect of summoning of respondents herein after considering the material on record.
Revision petition stands disposed of in said terms.
